Reason: Westermark's sign is a radiographic indicator of pulmonary embolism characterized by focal oligemia, which presents as an area of increased translucency (hyperlucency) due to reduced or absent vascular markings distal to the occlusion. The image shows the right lung is more lucent than the left with paucity of vessels, fitting this description.
